title: Activated fibroblasts modify keratinocyte stem niche through TET1 and IL-6 to promote their rapid transformation in a mouse model of prenatal arsenic exposure.
ehr_evidence: BALB/c female mice, aged five weeks, were acquired from the animal rearing facility at the CSIR- Indian Institute of Toxicology Research.
summary: In vivo and in vitro study examining how prenatal arsenic exposure in mice activates dermal fibroblasts to secrete IL-6, which modifies the keratinocyte stem cell niche via TET1-mediated epigenetic changes and JAK2/STAT3 signaling, promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition and skin tumorigenesis.
key_findings: Prenatal arsenic exposure increased α-SMA positive cells in offspring skin at PND 2 (37 ± 2.7) and 18 weeks (26.2 ± 2.6) compared to controls.
Conditioned media from exposed fibroblasts increased IL-6 levels (MFI 7919 ± 350.4 vs 4086 ± 50.4) and reduced KSC apoptosis (2 ± 0.3% vs 10.4 ± 0.5%).
KSCs cultured in exposed fibroblast media showed increased proliferation (BrdU uptake 11.2 ± 0.7% vs 3 ± 0.8%) and EMT markers (N-cadherin 1.6 ± 1.2 fold, Vimentin 2.9 ± 1.8 fold).
TET1 protein increased 1.8 ± 0.06 fold and IL-6 mRNA increased 8.1 ± 1.4 fold in exposed fibroblasts, with an 8.4 ± 1.5% rise in 5-hmC/5-mC ratio at the IL-6 promoter.
study_design: in vivo mouse model and in vitro cell culture study
data_source_type: animal model / in vitro cell culture
population: BALB/c mice (prenatally exposed to arsenic and control offspring), primary dermal fibroblasts and keratinocyte stem cells
limitations: animal model may not fully recapitulate human pathophysiology
in vitro conditioned media does not fully replicate the complex in vivo microenvironment
data_availability_statement: The datasets generated and analyzed during the current study are submitted to CSIR-IITR repository and will be made available by corresponding author on request.
